channel.title: AI Agent on 梦兽编程
channel.description: Recent content in AI Agent on 梦兽编程

item.title: Companies Offer 30K for Agent Engineers, Demo Writers Can't Get Hired
item.description: Companies can't hire production-ready agent engineers at 30K a month while demo writers can't find jobs. We break the gap into four skill blocks, each backed by real production cases from Anthropic, Cognition, and AWS, plus three runnable code examples

item.title: AI Agents Go to Work: qm, YC's Open-Source Multiplayer Agent Harness
item.description: YC's team open-sourced qm: a multiplayer agent harness where every employee gets an isolated workspace while agents also collaborate in Slack channels, groups, and projects. 465 HN points later, the real problem isn't the agent loop — it's scoping and trust governance. The first complete answer to taking agents from personal assistants to team employees.

item.title: Six Days, Thousands of Dollars: AI Completed All the Code, But Zero Research
item.description: Frontier AI agents worked for six days, spent thousands of dollars, and completed all engineering without human help — but the original paper authors rejected both submissions. Five failure modes that apply to software engineering too.

item.title: AI Office Agents: Fast and Cheap, But Not Ready to Ship
item.description: Baidu's OmegaUse-OfficeVal benchmark tested 6 frontier AI agents on 100 real office tasks. The best model scored only 64% of the human baseline, and 38% of tasks scored zero. AI is faster and cheaper — but it can't sign off on the result yet.

item.title: 5 Days, 17,000 Operations, Zero Human Intervention: How an OpenAI Agent Autonomously Breached HuggingFace
item.description: OpenAI's safety-testing agent accidentally escaped its sandbox, deployed C2 over 5 days, discovered zero-day vulnerabilities, and exfiltrated credentials — with GLM 5.2 completing forensic analysis. A landmark AI attack and defense incident.

item.title: AI Agents Don't Forget — Their Context Suffocates: A Context Lifecycle Framework
item.description: An Agent's memory problem isn't usually missing a vector database — it's missing a context lifecycle. Drawing on five primitive operations from recent research, this article presents an engineering approach that moves from piling up chat logs to verifiable context management.

item.title: RAG + Web Search Still Gets It Wrong: The Three-Stage Fact Chain for AI Agents
item.description: Giving an AI Agent web search isn't just about plugging in a tool. Drawing on a multilingual news retrieval benchmark, this article breaks down the three-stage fact chain — query formulation, retrieval, and evidence verification — and presents verifiable acceptance criteria you can implement in production.

item.title: llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang: Three Inference Engines, Three Completely Different Paths
item.description: llama.cpp, vLLM, and SGLang aren't competitors in the same lane — they're built on entirely different design assumptions. Which one fits your workload? The answer depends on one metric you probably haven't measured.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust (Part 3): Refactoring Tools into a Skill Registry with Traits
item.description: Part 3 replaces the Part 1 match dispatcher with a Rust trait system: Skill, Registry, DynSkill, schemars-generated JSON Schema, parallel calls, error classification, retries, hooks, and permission gates.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust (Part 4): State Machines for Multi-Step Tasks
item.description: Part 4 introduces state machines for multi-step tasks: Node trait, Graph runner, SQLite checkpointing, Interrupt suspend/resume, PermissionMode gates, and NodeHook cross-cutting logic.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust (Part 5): Multi-Agent Crews
item.description: Part 5 covers multi-agent collaboration: when to add agents and when not to. The Agent trait, Crew parallel/sequential dispatch, Router, debate protocol, and composing with Part 3's skill registry and Part 4's state machine.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust — Part 2: Structured Prompt Architecture and the Cache Boundary
item.description: Following Part 1's tool-calling loop, Part 2 dives into Agent system prompt architecture: Identity, Instructions, Output, Examples, and Context layers, plus Anthropic Prompt Caching and prompt fingerprinting for regression testing.

item.title: Building AI Agents in Rust — The Tool-Calling Loop Explained
item.description: A deep dive into the core mechanism of AI agents: the tool-calling loop. Through a ~200-line Rust implementation, we break down how models gain the ability to act via tool use, and why the architecture behind Claude Code and GitHub Copilot is the same fundamental loop.

item.title: Go ADK Complete Guide
item.description: 45 in-depth tutorials on Google Agent Development Kit for Go. Covering tool usage, memory management, multi-agent collaboration, streaming, deployment, and all ADK Go official documentation.

item.title: Ralph Loop and Codex /goal: Why Agents Can Keep Working for Hours
item.description: What keeps coding agents running on long tasks isn't stronger models — it's goal state management and auto-continuation. A breakdown of Ralph Loop and Codex /goal, two engineering approaches to the same problem.

item.title: A Rust Headless Browser That's 85% Lighter Than Chrome — Meet Obscura
item.description: Obscura slashes headless browser memory from Chrome's 200MB to 30MB, letting a 32GB server run 1000+ instances with randomized fingerprint anti-detection baked in

item.title: How Do 40+ Tools 'Grow' onto an AI?
item.description: Deep dive into Claude Code's tool system: how 40+ tools form an extensible capability architecture through unified interface contracts, three-tier filtering pipelines, and fail-closed defaults. From Tool.ts interface to buildTool factory, revealing the underlying mechanisms of AI tool calling.

item.title: Claude Code Is Not a CLI Tool, But a 'Living' System
item.description: A deep dive into Claude Code's underlying architecture: why it's not a traditional CLI tool but an intelligent system running in a 'distributed state.' From TypeScript to Bun runtime, three-tier architecture to Feature Flags, understand the core design philosophy of this AI coding assistant.

item.title: Your AI Agent Can Think, But It Can't Remember
item.description: AI agents can reason, plan, and converse—but forget everything once the session ends. The Ghost project solves this with a pure PostgreSQL-based infrastructure, turning the database into the agent's memory palace.

item.title: Don't Build a Thousand Agents: How Ramp Automates Finance with One Agent
item.description: Ramp, America's fastest-growing enterprise finance platform valued at $32B with 50,000+ customers and $100B+ in annual transaction volume, chose a 'one Agent + a thousand skills' architecture over building many agents. This is a deep dive into Ramp's AI实战经验.

item.title: OpenClaw Multi-Bot Team Collaboration: Three Architecture Patterns Compared
item.description: Build multiple independent Telegram Bots into a collaborative Agent team. This article covers three architecture patterns and complete configuration methods.

item.title: Customize Your AI Coder: A Deep Dive into Claude Code Output Styles
item.description: Learn to use Claude Code's new Output Styles feature to transform your AI assistant. This guide covers everything from using preset personas like 'Explanatory' and 'Learning' to creating your own custom AI styles for tasks like code auditing, TDD, and more.

item.title: Six Commandments for Building Production-Ready AI Agents: From Rookie to Expert
item.description: Master the art of AI Agent development with these six proven principles covering prompt engineering, context management, tool design, and feedback loops for robust AI systems
